## Summary

A method tweet: find time-of-day/weekday structure in any market with **no indicators**, in ~60 seconds. The process ("market mapping"):

1. Load 15 years of 60-minute data.
2. Map **every entry hour × exit hour × day of the week** combination.
3. Color the grid by net profit.
4. Filter for **average trade size** and **profit/drawdown ratio**.
5. Check a **robustness index**: does the edge survive shifting entry/exit by 1–3 hours?
6. Confirm it still holds in the **last 1–3 years** (recency).

The claimed payoff: on E-mini NASDAQ this "immediately surfaces strong structural tendencies, especially Mondays and certain overnight holds." Clean example: **enter 6am → exit 4pm (or longer) every Monday** — the edge survives time shifts and remains valid recently. Framed as "the market's own built-in time tendencies," not indicator curves; trade the window standalone or drop a breakout strategy inside it.

## Why it matters

- **The grid IS the idea, and it's implementable today.** Our backtest line ([[2026-08-30-ignis-trend-following-realtest]], [[2026-08-29-three-simple-ma-atr-systems]]) already has the data; the map is a group-by over entry-hour × exit-hour × weekday — cheap to compute, and a genuinely different discovery lens from the signal-based systems we usually capture.
- **But it is the most multiple-testing-heavy method in this genre.** 24 entry hours × 24 exit hours × 5 weekdays ≈ **2,880 cells per market**, then colored and filtered by performance. The best cell out of ~3,000 looks impressive *by construction* — the day-of-week/hour genre Peter warns about in [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]]. Any replication must lead with a multiplicity haircut (White's Reality Check / deflated-Sharpe logic — [[2026-10-24-dmartin-deflated-sharpe-ratio]]), not the raw grid.
- **The tweet's own guards are half-right.** The ±1–3h robustness shift and the last-1–3-years check are real discipline (same family as [[2026-10-21-setupalpha-trend-system-robustness-tests]]) — but adjacent grid cells are highly correlated, so surviving a time shift is weaker protection than it sounds, and the last-3-years check happens *after* selection on the full 15y, so it isn't clean out-of-sample.
- **Tension worth noting:** the flagship example is a **Monday long** on NASDAQ futures (6am→4pm+). Our closest captured cousin is the opposite trade — [[2026-10-01-algojan-nq-monday-short]] (short NQ Monday when Friday's high unbroken, +573% claimed, 22.6% win rate). Same market, same day, opposite direction — both can't be unconditionally true; whichever window wins, the condition/detail is doing all the work. That contrast is exactly why the grid needs mechanism + haircut before belief.
- **Source context:** 5 likes / 282 views, marketing handle ("Academy") — this is a product-demo tweet for their grid software; the screenshot is the product, which explains the "60 seconds" hook. Method still stands on its own merits.
